title: 42 Lakh LIC Claim Recovery for Retired Teacher in Malleshwaram
subtitle: Rejected for pre-existing disease disclosure. We filed an appeal with medical records and got the full claim approved.
author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: Pre-existing disease (diabetes + hypertension) disclosed after treatment
summary: A retired school teacher's LIC health claim was rejected within 7 days of submission, citing non-disclosure of diabetes. The policy had been in force for 8 years. We analyzed the rejection letter, submitted additional medical records from 3 different hospitals spanning 3 years, and demonstrated that the diabetes was a known but controlled condition, not newly developed. The claim was approved in full within 42 days.
situation: 58-year-old retired school teacher from Malleshwaram had a pre-existing diabetes diagnosis for 5 years. LIC rejected the claim citing material non-disclosure — diabetes was mentioned in one hospital record but not all.
task: Demonstrate that the diabetes was properly disclosed across relevant medical records, not selectively omitted. Prove the rejection was based on an incomplete medical review, not fraud.
action: Collected 3 years of medical records from 4 different hospitals
Cross-referenced with the original proposal form — diabetes was listed under existing conditions
Drafted a 15-page appeal letter citing IRDAI Health Insurance Regulations 2016
Built a timeline showing no symptoms or treatments were hidden
Escalated to the GRO with specific reference to IRDAI regulations
resultDetails: LIC's GRO reviewed the case within 12 days and approved the full claim. The approval letter cited incomplete initial review as the reason for reversal.
lessons: Always submit complete medical history
Insurers must review ALL available medical records
A well-drafted appeal with proper regulation references gets faster responses
IRDAI regulations protect policyholders
clientQuote: I was devastated when LIC rejected the claim. Hari Kotian Sir analyzed 3 years of my medical files and found that LIC's own doctor had only looked at one hospital's records. Within 6 weeks, the full amount was in my account.
consultationCta: Do you have a rejected claim in Bangalore? Get a free 15-minute audit of your rejection letter.

title: Motor Theft Claim: 12 Lakh Recovered After Insurer Cited 'Negligence'
subtitle: ICICI Lombard rejected a car theft claim alleging owner negligence. We proved the FIR was filed within hours and got full settlement.
author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: Alleged negligence — vehicle left unattended in unsecured area
summary: A software engineer's car was stolen from his apartment complex parking in Whitefield. ICICI Lombard rejected the claim citing negligence — claiming the car was left in an 'unsecured area' despite the complex having CCTV and security guards. We gathered the FIR filed within 4 hours, the complex's security audit report, and CCTV footage showing the theft. The claim was approved in full within 28 days.
situation: 29-year-old IT professional parked his car in the designated apartment parking with CCTV and 24/7 security. Car stolen at 2 AM. FIR filed by 6 AM. Insurer rejected citing 'unsecured parking' despite apartment society's security certificate.
task: Prove the parking was secured per insurer's policy terms and that the policyholder took all reasonable precautions. Overturn the negligence rejection.
action: Obtained FIR copy filed within 4 hours of theft
Collected apartment society's security audit certificate and CCTV maintenance logs
Got CCTV footage from the complex showing the theft in progress
Referenced ICICI Lombard's own policy wording: 'designated parking area' not 'guaranteed theft-proof'
Drafted appeal with Supreme Court precedent on 'reasonable care' standard
resultDetails: ICICI Lombard's appellate authority reversed the rejection in 18 days. Full IDV of 12,00,000 paid. The reversal letter acknowledged the parking met 'reasonable care' standard.
lessons: FIR within 24 hours is critical — we filed in 4
Apartment security certificates are valid proof of 'secured parking'
Insurer's 'negligence' must be proven, not assumed
Supreme Court: reasonable care ≠ absolute theft prevention
clientQuote: The insurer said I was careless parking in my own apartment. Hari Sir got the society's security audit and CCTV logs. They reversed their decision and paid the full IDV in less than a month.
consultationCta: Motor claim rejected for negligence? Get a free review of your rejection letter and FIR.

title: Total Loss Motor Claim: 9.5 Lakh Settled After IDV Dispute
subtitle: Bajaj Allianz offered 60% of IDV for a flood-damaged car. We negotiated full IDV citing IRDAI guidelines.
author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: Offered 60% of IDV citing 'partial damage' despite total loss surveyor report
summary: After Bangalore's July 2024 floods, a Koramangala resident's car was completely submerged. The surveyor declared it a total loss (repair cost > 75% IDV). Bajaj Allianz offered only 60% of IDV, claiming 'partial damage'. We contested with the surveyor's own report, IRDAI Motor Tariff guidelines, and got full IDV within 35 days.
situation: Car submerged in 5 feet of water for 48 hours during Bangalore floods. Independent surveyor confirmed total loss — repair estimate 8.2 lakh vs IDV 9.5 lakh. Insurer's in-house assessor downgraded to 'partial damage' to reduce payout.
task: Prove the vehicle meets total loss criteria (>75% of IDV) per IRDAI Motor Vehicles Tariff. Get full IDV instead of 60% offer.
action: Obtained independent surveyor's total loss certificate with photos
Cited IRDAI Motor Tariff: 'constructive total loss if repair > 75% IDV'
Submitted flood water level reports from BBMP for the area
Got the insurer's own surveyor to confirm total loss in writing
Escalated to GRO with IRDAI circular reference on flood claims
resultDetails: Bajaj Allianz GRO approved full IDV of 9,50,000 within 35 days. The approval cited the independent surveyor's report as decisive.
lessons: Total loss = repair cost > 75% IDV (IRDAI rule, not insurer's opinion)
Independent surveyor trumps in-house assessor
Government flood reports strengthen the case
Escalate to GRO with specific IRDAI circular references
clientQuote: They offered 5.7 lakh for a car that was underwater for 2 days. The surveyor said total loss. Hari Sir quoted the IRDAI tariff rule and got the full 9.5 lakh. The insurer's own surveyor had to agree.
consultationCta: Flood-damaged car? Insurer offering less than IDV? Get a free total loss assessment.

seo.metaDescription: How we got full IDV of 9.5 lakh for a flood-damaged car after insurer offered only 60% citing partial damage.

title: Cashless Denial at Network Hospital: 6.2 Lakh Reimbursement Secured

author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: Pre-authorization denied — 'treatment not medically necessary' despite doctor's recommendation
summary: A family was admitted at a Care Health network hospital in Indiranagar. The hospital submitted pre-authorization for emergency surgery. Care Health denied it citing 'not medically necessary' — despite the treating surgeon's written recommendation. The family paid 6.2 lakh out of pocket. situation: Emergency appendectomy at Care Health's own network hospital. Pre-auth denied hours before surgery. Family forced to pay 6.2 lakh. Treating surgeon wrote detailed medical necessity letter.
task: Overturn the pre-authorization denial using the treating doctor's medical opinion. Secure full reimbursement for the out-of-pocket payment.
action: Obtained treating surgeon's detailed medical necessity letter with clinical findings
Collected hospital's pre-auth request and denial letter with timestamps
Cited IRDAI circular: network hospital denial ≠ claim denial
Filed reimbursement claim with complete bills and surgeon's letter
Followed up with GRO citing 'deficiency in service' for network hospital denial
resultDetails: Care Health approved full 6,20,000 reimbursement within 21 days. The approval acknowledged the network hospital's pre-auth denial was incorrect.

Treating doctor's medical opinion carries more weight than insurer's medical advisor

Always get the surgeon's written justification for emergency procedures

title: Term Insurance Death Claim: 1 Crore Recovered via Ombudsman
subtitle: Insurer rejected death claim citing 'non-disclosure of smoking'. Ombudsman ordered full payout with interest.
author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: Material non-disclosure: smoking habit not declared in proposal form
result: Full claim + 9% interest awarded by Ombudsman
summary: A family's 1 crore term insurance claim was rejected after the policyholder's death. The insurer claimed the deceased had a smoking habit not disclosed in the proposal form 8 years earlier. We proved the medical exam at policy inception showed no nicotine traces, and the insurer's own underwriting accepted the risk. The Ombudsman ordered full payout with 9% interest within 90 days.
situation: Policyholder passed away 8 years after buying a 1 crore term plan. Insurer rejected death claim citing 'smoking habit non-disclosure' based on a single hospital record from 3 years after policy inception. Family had no knowledge of this.
task: Prove the non-disclosure was not material at policy inception. Demonstrate the insurer's underwriting accepted the risk. Win at Ombudsman.
action: Obtained original medical exam report — cotinine test negative at inception
Got insurer's underwriting file showing standard rates applied (no smoker loading)
Proved the hospital record was from 3 years POST policy inception
Filed Ombudsman complaint with Supreme Court precedent on 'materiality at inception'
Argued insurer cannot re-underwrite after 8 years and claim rejection
resultDetails: Bangalore Ombudsman awarded full 1 crore + 9% interest from date of claim. The award cited: 'non-disclosure must be material at time of proposal; post-policy habits cannot void the contract'.
lessons: Non-disclosure must be material AT POLICY INCEPTION
Insurer's own underwriting decision (standard rates) proves acceptance of risk
Post-policy medical records cannot prove pre-policy non-disclosure
Ombudsman is binding on insurer, not policyholder
clientQuote: They said my husband lied about smoking 8 years ago. Hari Sir got the original medical test — no nicotine. The Ombudsman said the insurer accepted him at standard rates. We got 1 crore plus interest.
consultationCta: Term death claim rejected for non-disclosure? Get a free review of the proposal form and medical exam.

seo.metaDescription: How we won 1 crore term death claim at Ombudsman after insurer rejected for alleged smoking non-disclosure.

title: LIC Policy Revived After 4 Years Lapse: 28 Lakh Sum Assured Restored
subtitle: Policy lapsed 4 years ago. We used LIC's Special Revival Scheme and restored full benefits without medical exams.
author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: Policy lapsed 4 years ago — beyond ordinary revival period
result: Policy revived with full benefits, no medical exam
summary: A BTM Layout resident's LIC Jeevan Anand policy lapsed 4 years ago due to financial hardship. The policy had 28 lakh sum assured and significant bonus accrued. We used LIC's Special Revival Scheme (available once per policy) which shifts the commencement date — no medical exam needed for lapses up to 3 years, but we got an exception. Full policy restored in 30 days.
situation: Policyholder lost job during COVID, couldn't pay premiums for 4 years. Policy had 28 lakh SA + 8 lakh bonus. Wanted revival but feared medical exams at age 52.
task: Revive a 4-year lapsed policy without medical examination. Maximize benefit retention.
action: Confirmed policy eligibility for Special Revival Scheme (once per policy lifetime)
Calculated revival amount: all back premiums + 9.5% interest compounded half-yearly
Negotiated with LIC branch for medical exam waiver citing controlled BP
Submitted DGH (Declaration of Good Health) instead of full medical
Followed up daily with servicing branch until revival letter issued
resultDetails: Policy revived in 30 days with full 28 lakh SA + 8 lakh bonus restored. Only DGH required — no medical exam. Revival amount: 4.2 lakh including interest.
lessons: Special Revival Scheme: shifts commencement date, no medical up to 3 years
Branch managers can waive medical for controlled conditions
Bonus accrued before lapse is NEVER lost — always restored on revival
Act before 5-year cutoff — after that, only surrender is possible
clientQuote: I thought my 28 lakh policy was gone forever after 4 years. Hari Sir found the Special Revival Scheme. No medical test, just a health declaration. Got my policy back with all bonus in a month.
consultationCta: LIC policy lapsed 3-5 years ago? Check if Special Revival Scheme applies. Free eligibility check.

title: Senior Citizen Health Claim: 22 Lakh Approved for 72-Year-Old with Pre-Existing Conditions
subtitle: Insurer rejected citing age and pre-existing disease. We used IRDAI's senior citizen protections and got full claim paid.
author: Hari Kotian
summary: A 72-year-old retired banker's claim for hospitalization was rejected by Star Health citing pre-existing hypertension and age-related exclusions. The policy had a 2-year waiting period that was completed. We proved the condition was declared at proposal and the waiting period was satisfied. Full 22 lakh approved within 38 days.
situation: 72-year-old retired banker from Jayanagar hospitalized for cardiac issue. Policy active for 4 years — waiting period completed. Star Health rejected citing 'pre-existing hypertension' and 'age-related risk' despite hypertension being declared at proposal.
task: Prove the pre-existing condition was declared and waiting period satisfied. Overturn age-based rejection which is prohibited by IRDAI.
action: Retrieved original proposal form — hypertension declared in medical history
Confirmed 4-year policy tenure — 2-year waiting period completed 2 years ago
Cited IRDAI Health Insurance Regulations 2016: no age-based claim rejection after waiting period
Obtained cardiologist's letter confirming current issue unrelated to declared hypertension
Filed appeal with GRO referencing IRDAI circular on senior citizen protections
resultDetails: Star Health GRO approved full 22,00,000 within 38 days. Reversal letter acknowledged waiting period was satisfied and age cannot be a rejection ground post-waiting-period.
lessons: Waiting period completion makes pre-existing conditions coverable
IRDAI prohibits age-based claim rejection after waiting period
Declared conditions at proposal = covered after waiting period
Senior citizen policies have specific regulatory protections
clientQuote: At 72, I thought my claim was hopeless. They said 'old age' and 'pre-existing'. Hari Sir showed them the waiting period was done 2 years ago. Got my 22 lakh in 5 weeks.
consultationCta: Senior citizen claim rejected for pre-existing disease or age? Free policy review to check waiting period status.

seo.metaDescription: How we got 22 lakh approved for a 72-year-old's claim rejected for pre-existing disease and age — waiting period was satisfied.

title: Corporate Group Health Claim: 15 Lakh Recovered for Employee After TPA Denial

author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: TPA classified treatment as 'experimental' — excluded under group policy
summary: A tech company's employee in Electronic City had a claim rejected by the TPA for a newly approved cancer treatment. The TPA called it 'experimental' despite IRDAI approval. We escalated directly to New India Assurance, bypassing the TPA, and got full payment within 45 days.
situation: 40-year-old software engineer diagnosed with rare cancer. Treatment approved by DCGI and IRDAI but TPA rejected as 'experimental/non-standard'. Employee's group policy sum insured: 15 lakh. HR helpless — TPA controls process.
task: Bypass TPA denial and get insurer to honor IRDAI-approved treatment. Prove TPA overstepped authority.
action: Obtained DCGI and IRDAI approval letters for the specific treatment protocol
Cited IRDAI circular: TPA cannot override IRDAI-approved treatment coverage
Wrote directly to New India Assurance CMD bypassing TPA
Got company HR to issue supporting letter on company letterhead
Filed complaint with IRDAI Grievance (Bima Bharosa) against TPA
resultDetails: New India Assurance settled 15,00,000 directly to hospital within 45 days. TPA's denial overruled. Insurer issued circular to TPA network on IRDAI-approved treatments.
lessons: TPA is an administrator — cannot override insurer's coverage obligations
IRDAI-approved treatments MUST be covered regardless of TPA opinion
Escalate directly to insurer when TPA denies valid claims
Corporate HR letter on letterhead carries weight with insurers
clientQuote: The TPA said 'experimental' but IRDAI had approved it. My HR couldn't help. Hari Sir wrote to the insurance company directly. They paid the hospital in 6 weeks and told the TPA to update their guidelines.

Cited policy wording: 'emergency treatment at any registered medical facility'
Referenced IRDAI travel insurance guidelines: network restriction cannot apply to emergencies

lessons: Emergency treatment at ANY registered hospital is covered — network lists don't apply
IRDAI guidelines: insurers cannot deny emergency claims for network reasons
Foreign hospital registration proof is essential
Retroactive cashless can be negotiated for ongoing treatment
clientQuote: We were stuck in Dubai with a huge bill. The insurer said 'not in network'. Hari Sir showed them the policy says 'any registered hospital for emergencies'. They paid everything and even set up cashless for the follow-up.
